content.overview: Section 31 allows prescribed classes of companies to file a shelf prospectus with the Registrar, valid for a prescribed period, and to make multiple offers without a fresh prospectus each time, subject to filing an information memorandum before each subsequent offer.
content.glance: Shelf prospectus for prescribed companies; validity period; information memorandum before later offers; updates and material changes.
content.study: A shelf prospectus is a prospectus in respect of which securities or classes of securities included therein are issued for subscription in one or more issues over a certain period without the issue of a further prospectus. Prescribed companies may file a shelf prospectus with the Registrar. Before a second or subsequent offer under the shelf prospectus, the company must file an information memorandum with the Registrar containing material facts relating to new charges, changes in financial position and other prescribed changes. Where an information memorandum is filed, every such memorandum together with the shelf prospectus is deemed to be a prospectus. Current-law framing: confirm the company is within the prescribed class; check validity period; require information memorandum for subsequent offers.

sections.heading: Shelf Prospectus
sections.body: Prescribed companies may file a shelf prospectus covering one or more issues over a stated validity period without a fresh prospectus for each issue.

sections.heading: Information Memorandum
sections.body: Before a subsequent offer under the shelf prospectus, an information memorandum updating material facts must be filed with the Registrar.

sections.heading: Deemed Prospectus
sections.body: The shelf prospectus together with each information memorandum is deemed to be a prospectus.

examples.title: Multiple issues under shelf
examples.body: A prescribed company files a shelf prospectus and later makes a second offer after filing an information memorandum with updated material facts. Section 31 is followed.

examples.title: Subsequent offer without information memorandum
examples.body: A company makes a second offer under a shelf prospectus without filing the information memorandum. Section 31 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Does a shelf prospectus remove all disclosure for later issues?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. An information memorandum updating material facts must be filed before each subsequent offer; together with the shelf prospectus it is deemed a prospectus.

distinctions.title: Shelf prospectus (s. 31) vs ordinary prospectus (s. 26)
distinctions.left: One filing covers multiple issues over a validity period with update memoranda
distinctions.right: Full prospectus for a single issue with complete s. 26 content

misconceptions.trap: Once a shelf prospectus is filed, no further disclosure is needed for later offers.
misconceptions.correction: An information memorandum must be filed before each subsequent offer.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 31 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm prescribed class. II. Check shelf filing and validity. III. Require information memorandum for subsequent offers. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Company class; shelf status; information memorandum compliance; precise relief.

examTips: State validity period and information memorandum.
Emphasise deemed-prospectus effect of shelf + memorandum.

enhancement.definition: Section 31 permits prescribed companies to use a shelf prospectus for multiple issues during a validity period, subject to filing an information memorandum before subsequent offers.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A shelf prospectus reduces repeated full prospectus filings while preserving updated disclosure through information memoranda.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 31 facilitates repeated capital raising with continuous disclosure updates.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm eligibility; check shelf and memoranda; apply deemed-prospectus consequences.
